subject: Tenant egress IP atlas + PrivateLink decision (FinBank) - post-call recap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@finbank.com>, Alex Li <alex.li@finbank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenant egress IP atlas + PrivateLink decision (FinBank) - post-call recap

Hi Samir / Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the Private VPC path and the networking asks we discussed.

Summary of your stated preference:
- Primary: Private VPC via AWS PrivateLink (preferred for traffic isolation and no peering exposure)
- Fallback: VPC Peering only if AWS setup blocks PrivateLink for any reason
- Egress model: FinBank wants fixed egress IPs per tenant for allowlisting; FinBank netops will supply the official CIDR/allowlist once we confirm ownership model

Open technical questions we need to resolve (I've put owners in parentheses):
1) Who initiates the PrivateLink endpoint (Redwood or FinBank)? We suggested Redwood can create and manage the endpoint service, but FinBank must create the VPC endpoint in their account (Jordan)
2) TLS / SNI expectations when connections originate from FinBank to our endpoint (Neha)
3) Egress IP mapping: whether FinBank expects one static IP per tenant or a pooled set per environment (Samir to confirm)
4) Firewall rules and NAT behavior for outbound callbacks (if any) — we need specific ports and destination IPs (Alex to share)

Attachments I’m sharing with this note:
- egres_cidrs_template.csv (template for FinBank to fill with tenant→CIDR mapping; small CSV)
- redwood-privatelink-setup.pdf (our PrivateLink implementation notes and roles)

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- Samir / Alex: populate the attached CSV with tenant->CIDR or confirm you want Redwood-managed egress IPs (ETA: 48 business hours)
- Neha: produce a short checklist (network acceptance criteria) that FinBank can sign off on once CIDRs are provided (ETA: 2 business days after we receive CIDRs)
- Vanessa: draft a brief SOW blurb for the Private VPC enablement (to support procurement) (ETA: 3 business days)

If we can get the egress CIDR mapping this week we can scope a PrivateLink pilot in early December.

Thanks — please reply inline if anything here is off.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood attachments: egres_cidrs_template.csv, redwood-privatelink-setup.pdf

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant egress IP atlas + PrivateLink decision (FinBank) - post-call recap

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from NetOps side (copied Alex & procurement):

1) CIDR mapping: we prefer a /29 (8 IPs) per tenant where possible; if you require pooling that’s OK but we need a published mapping per environment. I attached a filled CSV for two pilot tenants.
2) PrivateLink initiation: FinBank will create the VPC Endpoint in our account (we generally manage endpoint resources). Would you be able to publish an endpoint service and share the service name and ARN?
3) Egress ownership: We prefer Redwood to provide managed egress IPs for outbound model calls (helps with scaling). Can you confirm if Redwood supports assigning a stable egress NAT IP per tenant when running PrivateLink?
4) TLS/SNI & ALPN: we expect mTLS for the tunnel, SNI header preserved, and ALPN set to h2 for HTTP/2. Any incompatible requirements will be a blocker.

I attached: egress_cidrs_finbank.csv (tenant_id,preferred_cidr) with two pilot rows.

Samir
Samir Shah
Senior Network Engineer, FinBank
samir.shah@finbank.com | +1 (212) 555-9842

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenant egress IP atlas + PrivateLink decision (FinBank) - post-call recap

Samir — perfect, thanks for the CSV and the details. Quick responses inline below and an updated ownership matrix attached.

- PrivateLink initiation: Redwood will publish the endpoint service and provide the service name/ARN. FinBank will create the endpoint in your VPC — we’ll supply the exact service name and a short validation checklist for your NetOps. (Owner: Jordan)
- Managed egress IPs: Redwood can offer a managed egress pool and map a stable NAT IP per tenant for the pilot. This will be an opt-in configuration; if you opt-in we’ll include the per-tenant NAT in the SOW. (Owner: Neha)
- mTLS / SNI / ALPN: Redwood supports mTLS to the PrivateLink endpoint. We preserve SNI and ALPN h2. We’ll include cipher suite requirements in the checklist. (Owner: Neha)
- Firewall & ports: For the pilot, allow outbound to our egress NAT IPs on 443 and 5222 (if you plan on websocket fallbacks). We will confirm final ports in the acceptance checklist.

Attached: ownership-matrix.xlsx (who does what), redwood-privatelink-setup.pdf (implementation steps), proposed-egress-list.csv (example of what our managed egress mapping looks like).

Next actions:
1) Samir: confirm you’re OK with Redwood-managed egress NAT for the pilot OR return the CSV with FinBank-managed CIDRs (you already sent two pilot rows — thanks).
2) Neha: I’ll need the short checklist from you by EOD Wednesday so we can hand to FinBank netops.
3) Vanessa: can you draft the short SOW blurb and get preliminary approval from procurement so we can attach it to the pilot proposal?

If all good I’ll upload these assets to the HubSpot record and loop procurement.

—
Jordan
